events.title: Rider Advocate brief: 7 claims (0 void)
events.body:
C1: The cancellation fee must be tested under NS-1, which requires all three of (i) the driver tapped "I'm Here", (ii) at the tap he was at the pickup point per GPS, and (iii) he waited more than 3 minutes (≥3:01) there; the system timeline shows the "I'm Here" tap condition is not reliably met and the within-200 m waiting time fell short of the threshold. [F6 F7 F2] [NS-0 NS-1]
C2: The GPS record contradicts the driver's claim: the driver went stationary from 13:02:25 to 13:05:40 (3 min 15 s) but his cumulative time within 200 m of the pickup before cancelling was only 4 min 30 s starting from 13:01:10, and after the 13:02:45 "I'm Here" tap he remained in range for only 2 min 55 s — under the 3:01 needed for NS-1(iii). [F3 F2 F6] [NS-1]
C3: Even if a tap occurred, NS-1(ii) requires GPS to place the driver at the pickup when he tapped; the only GPS position evidence (40 m / 38 m from pickup) shows he was near but the timeline field for the arrival tap is null, so condition (i) is not satisfied on the system record — and the records, not the driver's statement, win. [F1 F3 F6 F7 F12] [NS-1 NS-2]
C4: The driver cancelled 7 min 40 s after acceptance and 4 min 30 s after the platform-recorded arrival; the rider came out about a minute after the cancellation, so there was no no-show by the rider and the $6.61 cancellation fee of record should be refunded in full. [F4 F5 F8] [NS-2]
C5: The $6.61 corresponds to the published cancellation fee only (surge 1.0×, no surge uplift applies), so the refund amount is the full fee actually charged and is computable from the fare fact F8. [F8 F9] [NS-2 NS-7]

[F10 F11 F12 F6 F7 F2] [NS-1]
C7: No external cause excuses the shortfall: there were no traffic incidents on the route during the trip window and the weather was fair, so nothing explains the cancellation as a rider-caused no-show. [F13 F14 F15] [NS-1 NS-2]
Weaknesses: The driver did in fact come close and wait: GPS puts his closest approach at 38 m (F1) and he was stationary 3 min 15 s at 40 m from the pickup (F3), and the platform recorded arrival at 13:01:10 (F5) — the other side will argue this is a genuine 3-minute-plus wait at the pickup. | Cumulative time within 200 m was 4 min 30 s before cancellation (F2), which exceeds 3 minutes in total; the driver will use F2 to argue NS-1(iii) is met and that the deficit only appears if you measure from the 13:02:45 tap (F6). | The timeline itself is internally inconsistent — F6 records a tap at 13:02:45 while F7 says the tap field is null — so the driver may argue the null value in F7 is a data glitch rather than proof he never pressed "I'm Here". | The rider's own account ("I came out a minute after the driver cancelled") is a bare statement with no GPS record of the rider's position, so the rider's timing claim is not independently corroborated in the fact table. | The driver has a clean profile (rating 4.81, 0 disputes in 90 d, F17), which weakens any suggestion of deliberate fee abuse and makes a flag_account request hard to support.

events.title: Rider Advocate rebuttal: 8 points
events.body:
→ D1 (concedes): Conceded that the driver was near the pickup (F1, F5) — proximity is not in dispute; what D1 omits is that GPS never puts him at the pickup point and NS-1(ii) is only one of three cumulative conditions, so being 38 m away does not by itself meet the test. [F1 F5] [NS-1]
→ D2: D2 conflates two different clocks: F2's 4 min 30 s is cumulative time inside 200 m measured from 13:01:10, while NS-1(iii) asks whether the driver waited >3 minutes at the pickup after his arrival flag — measured from the 13:02:45 tap (F6) the in-range wait was only 2 min 55 s, below the 3:01 threshold. [F2 F3 F6] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D3: D3 rests on F6 alone while the same timeline's tap field is null (F7), so the record is self-contradictory and cannot be treated as unqualified proof of NS-1(i); a driver's own chat message (F10) cannot cure a missing system record, because system records win over statements. [F6 F7 F10] [NS-1]
→ D4: The 4 min 30 s gap in D4 runs from the platform-recorded arrival (F5), not from the arrival flag, and no clause treats the mere duration of stationarity as satisfying NS-1; his own message "Waited more than 3 min, cancelling" (F11) is a self-serving statement contradicted by the in-range timing in F6. [F5 F11 F6] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D5: The service type and the 1.0× surge (F9) are not in dispute, but NS-0 only routes a driver-cancellation to NS-1/NS-2; because F6/F7 fail condition (i) and the post-tap in-range wait of 2 min 55 s fails (iii), the $6.61 charged (F8) is not chargeable. [F8 F9 F6 F7] [NS-0 NS-1 NS-2]
→ D6: Absence of a rider chat message proves nothing: the fact table contains no rider-side GPS or message record at all, and the rider's account of coming out about a minute after cancellation is unrebutted by any record showing she was not coming; the burden of the three NS-1 conditions lies on the driver who presses the button. [F10 F11 F4] [NS-1 NS-7]
→ D7: D7 actually helps the rider: with no incidents (F14), only a normal 20–29 km/h band (F13) and fair weather (F15), there is no external cause explaining the cancellation, so no reason to shift the consequence onto the passenger. [F13 F14 F15] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D8 (concedes): We do not ask for flag_account and accept the driver's clean record (F17); we ask only for the $6.61 to be refunded under NS-2, which requires no misconduct finding — NS-2 applies whenever any NS-1 condition fails, and F6/F7 fail condition (i). [F17 F6 F7 F8] [NS-2 NS-7]
Revised ask: refund_full $6.61

points.response: Conceded that the driver was near the pickup (F1, F5) — proximity is not in dispute; what D1 omits is that GPS never puts him at the pickup point and NS-1(ii) is only one of three cumulative conditions, so being 38 m away does not by itself meet the test.

D2 conflates two different clocks: F2's 4 min 30 s is cumulative time inside 200 m measured from 13:01:10, while NS-1(iii) asks whether the driver waited >3 minutes at the pickup after his arrival flag — measured from the 13:02:45 tap (F6) the in-range wait was only 2 min 55 s, below the 3:01 threshold.

D3 rests on F6 alone while the same timeline's tap field is null (F7), so the record is self-contradictory and cannot be treated as unqualified proof of NS-1(i); a driver's own chat message (F10) cannot cure a missing system record, because system records win over statements.

The 4 min 30 s gap in D4 runs from the platform-recorded arrival (F5), not from the arrival flag, and no clause treats the mere duration of stationarity as satisfying NS-1; his own message "Waited more than 3 min, cancelling" (F11) is a self-serving statement contradicted by the in-range timing in F6.

The service type and the 1.0× surge (F9) are not in dispute, but NS-0 only routes a driver-cancellation to NS-1/NS-2; because F6/F7 fail condition (i) and the post-tap in-range wait of 2 min 55 s fails (iii), the $6.61 charged (F8) is not chargeable.

Absence of a rider chat message proves nothing: the fact table contains no rider-side GPS or message record at all, and the rider's account of coming out about a minute after cancellation is unrebutted by any record showing she was not coming; the burden of the three NS-1 conditions lies on the driver who presses the button.

D7 actually helps the rider: with no incidents (F14), only a normal 20–29 km/h band (F13) and fair weather (F15), there is no external cause explaining the cancellation, so no reason to shift the consequence onto the passenger.

We do not ask for flag_account and accept the driver's clean record (F17); we ask only for the $6.61 to be refunded under NS-2, which requires no misconduct finding — NS-2 applies whenever any NS-1 condition fails, and F6/F7 fail condition (i).

claims.assertion: The cancellation fee must be tested under NS-1, which requires all three of (i) the driver tapped "I'm Here", (ii) at the tap he was at the pickup point per GPS, and (iii) he waited more than 3 minutes (≥3:01) there; the system timeline shows the "I'm Here" tap condition is not reliably met and the within-200 m waiting time fell short of the threshold.

The GPS record contradicts the driver's claim: the driver went stationary from 13:02:25 to 13:05:40 (3 min 15 s) but his cumulative time within 200 m of the pickup before cancelling was only 4 min 30 s starting from 13:01:10, and after the 13:02:45 "I'm Here" tap he remained in range for only 2 min 55 s — under the 3:01 needed for NS-1(iii).

Even if a tap occurred, NS-1(ii) requires GPS to place the driver at the pickup when he tapped; the only GPS position evidence (40 m / 38 m from pickup) shows he was near but the timeline field for the arrival tap is null, so condition (i) is not satisfied on the system record — and the records, not the driver's statement, win.

The driver cancelled 7 min 40 s after acceptance and 4 min 30 s after the platform-recorded arrival; the rider came out about a minute after the cancellation, so there was no no-show by the rider and the $6.61 cancellation fee of record should be refunded in full.
The $6.61 corresponds to the published cancellation fee only (surge 1.0×, no surge uplift applies), so the refund amount is the full fee actually charged and is computable from the fare fact F8.

The driver's chat messages at 13:02 and 13:05 and his written statement assert he pressed "I'm Here" and waited over 3 minutes, but these are user-submitted statements contradicted by the GPS/timeline records on the within-200 m duration and the null arrival-tap field, so they cannot support the fee.
No external cause excuses the shortfall: there were no traffic incidents on the route during the trip window and the weather was fair, so nothing explains the cancellation as a rider-caused no-show.

weaknesses: The driver did in fact come close and wait: GPS puts his closest approach at 38 m (F1) and he was stationary 3 min 15 s at 40 m from the pickup (F3), and the platform recorded arrival at 13:01:10 (F5) — the other side will argue this is a genuine 3-minute-plus wait at the pickup.

Cumulative time within 200 m was 4 min 30 s before cancellation (F2), which exceeds 3 minutes in total; the driver will use F2 to argue NS-1(iii) is met and that the deficit only appears if you measure from the 13:02:45 tap (F6).

The timeline itself is internally inconsistent — F6 records a tap at 13:02:45 while F7 says the tap field is null — so the driver may argue the null value in F7 is a data glitch rather than proof he never pressed "I'm Here".

The rider's own account ("I came out a minute after the driver cancelled") is a bare statement with no GPS record of the rider's position, so the rider's timing claim is not independently corroborated in the fact table.
The driver has a clean profile (rating 4.81, 0 disputes in 90 d, F17), which weakens any suggestion of deliberate fee abuse and makes a flag_account request hard to support.

claims.assertion: The driver was physically at the pickup point when he cancelled: GPS puts his closest approach at 38 m from the pickup point (F1) and the platform's own timeline records his arrival at the pickup at 13:01:10 (F5).

The driver satisfied the waiting requirement of more than 3 minutes at the pickup point: he was stationary for 3 min 15 s (13:02:25–13:05:40) at 40 m from pickup (F3) and had been within 200 m of the pickup for a cumulative 4 min 30 s before cancelling (F2), both exceeding the 3:01 threshold.

The platform timeline shows the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 13:02:45 while 41 m from the pickup point, and he stayed within 200 m for a further 2 min 55 s after the tap (F6), so the arrival-flag condition was met; the chat confirming "I'm here at the pickup point" at 13:02 (F10) is consistent with that record.

The driver cancelled only after completing the wait: cancellation was recorded at 13:05:40, 4 min 30 s after the recorded arrival (F5) and after he messaged "Waited more than 3 min, cancelling" (F11); the $6.61 cancellation fee on record (F4, F8) is therefore valid for a rider no-show.

The service is RydeX (non-taxi), so the cancellation fee of $6.61 is chargeable under the rider no-show rule and does not depend on trip completion or on surge — the surge multiplier was 1.0x with no surge applied (F9).

The rider's assertion that she "came out a minute after the driver cancelled" is not supported by any chat message asking the driver to wait or announcing her arrival: the chat contains only the driver's arrival and cancellation messages (F10, F11), and there is no rider message in the record.

No mitigating event excused the rider's absence: no traffic incidents were recorded near the route during the trip window (F14), the only speed-band reading was a normal 20–29 km/h band (F13), and weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F15).

The driver has a 3.9-year account, 4.81 rating, 651 trips in 90 days and zero disputes or upheld complaints (F17), so there is no basis to attach a flag_account action for abuse of the waiting/cancellation button.

weaknesses: Timeline facts conflict with each other: F7 states the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), while F6 states a tap at 13:02:45 — the rider will rely on F7 to argue NS-1(i) fails and to invite a flag_account under NS-2.

On the driver's own account the rider did not board, and the gap between the recorded arrival (13:01:10, F5) and cancellation (13:05:40) is short — the rider will argue she was only seconds late, using her statement of coming out "a minute" later; her near-clean profile (4.9 rating, 0 disputes, 1460-day account, F16) supports an appeal under NS-7.

The strict NS-1(ii)/(iii) reading on the driving distance is arguable against us: the driver was stationary 40 m away (F3) and never reached 0 m, so the rider may contend he was not exactly "at the pick-up location" even though F1/F2 put him well within any arrival radius.

If the judge counts waiting time only from the "I'm Here" tap at 13:02:45 (F6), the in-range wait after the tap was 2 min 55 s (F6/F7 narrative), i.e. under the 3:01 threshold, which would flip the case to NS-2 and full refund.

points.response: Conceded that the driver was near the pickup (F1, F5) — proximity is not in dispute; what D1 omits is that GPS never puts him at the pickup point and NS-1(ii) is only one of three cumulative conditions, so being 38 m away does not by itself meet the test.

D2 conflates two different clocks: F2's 4 min 30 s is cumulative time inside 200 m measured from 13:01:10, while NS-1(iii) asks whether the driver waited >3 minutes at the pickup after his arrival flag — measured from the 13:02:45 tap (F6) the in-range wait was only 2 min 55 s, below the 3:01 threshold.

D3 rests on F6 alone while the same timeline's tap field is null (F7), so the record is self-contradictory and cannot be treated as unqualified proof of NS-1(i); a driver's own chat message (F10) cannot cure a missing system record, because system records win over statements.

The 4 min 30 s gap in D4 runs from the platform-recorded arrival (F5), not from the arrival flag, and no clause treats the mere duration of stationarity as satisfying NS-1; his own message "Waited more than 3 min, cancelling" (F11) is a self-serving statement contradicted by the in-range timing in F6.

The service type and the 1.0× surge (F9) are not in dispute, but NS-0 only routes a driver-cancellation to NS-1/NS-2; because F6/F7 fail condition (i) and the post-tap in-range wait of 2 min 55 s fails (iii), the $6.61 charged (F8) is not chargeable.

Absence of a rider chat message proves nothing: the fact table contains no rider-side GPS or message record at all, and the rider's account of coming out about a minute after cancellation is unrebutted by any record showing she was not coming; the burden of the three NS-1 conditions lies on the driver who presses the button.

D7 actually helps the rider: with no incidents (F14), only a normal 20–29 km/h band (F13) and fair weather (F15), there is no external cause explaining the cancellation, so no reason to shift the consequence onto the passenger.

We do not ask for flag_account and accept the driver's clean record (F17); we ask only for the $6.61 to be refunded under NS-2, which requires no misconduct finding — NS-2 applies whenever any NS-1 condition fails, and F6/F7 fail condition (i).

The three NS-1 conditions are met on the system records, not unmet: the platform records the arrival at 13:01:10 and an "I'm Here" tap at 13:02:45 while the driver was 41 m from the pickup (F5, F6), and the cumulative in-range time before cancelling was 4 min 30 s (F2).

The rider measures the wait only from the 13:02:45 tap, but NS-1(iii) is satisfied on the record: the driver was within 200 m for 4 min 30 s before cancelling (F2) and stationary 3 min 15 s at 40 m from the pickup (F3); the 2 min 55 s figure is merely the post-tap remainder of a longer in-range wait.

Condition (i) is documented: the timeline records the tap at 13:02:45 at 41 m from the pickup (F6), so the null entry in F7 is an internal record conflict, and the consistent record set (F2, F3, F5, F6) governs.

The rider's "one minute after" account is a bare statement with no GPS or timeline entry, while the position record shows the driver at the pickup from 13:01:10 and stationary there 3 min 15 s before cancelling at 13:05:40 (F3, F5); the no-show therefore stands.
The $6.61 is the published cancellation fee actually charged with no surge uplift (F8, F9); a valid rider no-show under NS-1 leaves that fee in place, so no amount is refundable.

The driver does not rely on his chat messages alone: the arrival, tap and waiting conditions are corroborated by system records F2, F3, F5 and F6, and the chat (F10, F11) only confirms the sequence those records already show.

Fair weather and no incidents (F13, F14, F15) remove external excuses, and that cuts against the rider too: with no incident, congestion or rain she had no reason not to reach a driver waiting 40 m away from 13:02:25 to 13:05:40 (F3).

Your driver cancelled the trip, and while they said you didn't show up, our records show they didn't wait long enough at the pickup for that to apply — the wait was six seconds short of what's required. Because of that, the $6.61 fee is refunded in full as a Ryde voucher. It'll be added to your account. Nothing else is needed from you, and no action was taken against the driver.

We reviewed the cancellation on this trip. We found you did arrive and tap at the pickup, and you were close enough to it — but the wait recorded there fell about six seconds short of the required three minutes before you cancelled. Because of that, the $6.61 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher and won't be paid to you. No action is being taken against your account, since your tap was at the pickup location and there's no sign of misuse.
